content: 1. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which is involved in its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of fluvoxamine by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP1A2, which is responsible for its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 3. Fostemsavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol through mechanisms involving inhibition of BCRP transporters. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Avoid coadministration or adjust the dose of BCRP substrates when used with fostemsavir. Do not exceed an ethinylestradiol dose of 30 mcg/day. 4. Gemifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Ethinylestradiol increases green tea levels by reducing its elimination. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of hemin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Drugs that increase delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may further reduce the effects of hemin. 8. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of hyaluronidase by rendering tissues partially resistant to its action when estrogens are administered in large systemic doses. Patients may require larger amounts of hyaluronidase for equivalent dispersing effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Iloperidone increases the levels of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A4. 10. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of insulin aspart through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 12. Norethindrone decreases the effects of insulin degludec through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. 13. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of insulin detemir, insulin glulisine, insulin lispro, insulin NPH, and regular human insulin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 14. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinylestradiol by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. At a dose of 40 mg/day, istradefylline increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials, but this effect was not observed at 20 mg/day. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. 16. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. CYP3A4 inhibitors like itraconazole may increase plasma hormone levels. 17. Norethindrone decreases the levels or effects of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Caution and monitoring are advised. Combination oral contraceptives significantly reduce plasma concentrations of lamotrigine, likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. 18. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. CYP3A4 inhibitors like ketoconazole may increase plasma hormone levels. 19. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is advised when coadministered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage adjustments. 21. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 22. Letermovir increases the levels of norethindrone by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. CYP3A4 inhibitors like ketoconazole may increase plasma hormone levels. 25. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of liraglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 26. Lixisenatide decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. GLP-1 agonists delay gastric emptying, which may affect the absorption of concomitantly administered oral medications. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least 1 hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. 27. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of lomitapide by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. The lomitapide dose should not exceed 30 mg/day. 28. Ethinylestradiol decreases the levels or effects of lonapegsomatropin by reducing serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) response to growth hormone analogs. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Higher growth hormone doses may be required. 29. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 31. Lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Norethindrone increases the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised due to the potential for increased toxicity. 33. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Norethindrone also decreases the effects of metformin through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 34. Metronidazole decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Mifepristone decreases the effects of norethindrone through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. A backup contraceptive method is recommended. 36. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP1A2. Caution and monitoring are advised. 37. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of midazolam by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ethinylestradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, increasing serum concentrations of concomitantly administered benzodiazepines. 38. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of intranasal midazolam by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration of mild CYP3A4 inhibitors with intranasal midazolam may cause higher systemic exposure, potentially prolonging sedation. 39. Mifepristone decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. A backup contraceptive method is recommended. 40. Minocycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 41. Mitotane decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; monitor for possible dosage adjustments when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates. 42. Momelotinib increases the toxicity of ethinylestradiol by competing for plasma protein binding. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Momelotinib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase exposure to BCRP substrates, raising the risk of adverse reactions. Dose adjustment of other BCRP substrates may be necessary. 43. Moxifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 44. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Nonhormonal contraceptives are recommended during therapy. 45. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Nemolizumab decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Nemolizumab suppresses cytokines, which may increase CYP enzyme activity. Monitor for decreased systemic levels of narrow therapeutic/sensitive CYP substrates after initiating nemolizumab. Dosage modification may be needed. 47. Neomycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 48. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 49. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 50. Nirmatrelvir decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing its metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Consider using additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods for the remainder of the cycle. The mechanism is unknown but may involve ritonavir-mediated CYP2C9 or CYP1A2 induction. 51. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing its metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Consider using additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods for the remainder of the cycle. The mechanism is unknown but may involve ritonavir-mediated CYP2C9 or CYP1A2 induction. 52. Nitrofurantoin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 53. Ofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised.
